summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a complex medical history including kidney transplant, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and prior empyema, was admitted for a persistent cough and mild weight gain. Evaluation revealed mild pulmonary edema and small bilateral pleural effusions on chest imaging, with CT findings of multifocal nodular airspace disease concerning for atypical pneumonitis. He was treated with IV diuresis for acute on chronic heart failure and transitioned to oral torsemide. Infectious workup, including negative urinary antigens and serum cryptococcal testing, did not confirm an active infection, and antibiotics were withheld due to improvement in symptoms and concern for C. difficile recurrence. Asymptomatic bacteriuria with Citrobacter koseri was noted but not treated per transplant guidelines. Tacrolimus was reduced from 2.5 mg to 2 mg twice daily due to an elevated level of 7.1. He improved clinically, with stable renal function and resolution of respiratory symptoms, and was discharged home with services and plans for outpatient follow-up with pulmonology and infectious disease.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Pleural effusion in other conditions classified elsewhere
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
